segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Owen Vane parted with his dispensing book as a man parts with a tooth, and only upon three conditions: that it be carried flat, that it be back upon his counter by Friday, and that nobody in Winchester be told whose shop it came out of. Judith agreed to two of these. She put it under her arm and walked down to the Bell before the light went.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Captain Farr heard her through without once interrupting, which was not a thing she was used to. When she came to the letter he set down his cup.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: April. She wrote in April, and burnt two before she got one to please her, and I was at Lisbon in April doing nothing whatever but learning to walk again.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: She had no direction but the regiment.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: The regiment would have found me. It found me with a bill from a bootmaker in Ipswich. And she gave it into his hand?

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: At the kitchen table, with the rest of the post. He had taken charge of it in March.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: Then I want Cobbold. His clerk drew the September will and his office has held my great-uncle's papers since before I was breeched. If there was ever an earlier one, it is on his shelf, and he will know it. I shall walk in Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: You will not walk eleven miles on that leg to be told to come back Thursday.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mr Rowe had come in behind her with the subscription book still under his coat, and had been standing by the settle working himself up to something for a full minute.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: Forgive me. Captain, forgive me, but you will go in alone, and you are a soldier nobody has seen these seven years, with no money, and a claim to three hundred a year. Any attorney in England hears that story twice a month. It is always told by a man who wants the farm.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: I do want the farm.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: Yes. That is precisely the trouble with it. But if Miss Vane went, and the book were in her keeping and not yours, and she said, my brother wrote this line and will swear to it, that is not a convenient story. That is a ledger in the hand of somebody who gets nothing whatever by it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He stopped, appalled at himself, and looked at the floor. Judith looked at him for rather longer than he liked.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: That is the first sensible thing anybody has said since Friday. I will go.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mrs Pike had it by nine the next morning, being at the Bell about a parcel she was not expecting, and gave her opinion in the yard where it would carry.

segments.speaker: Mrs Honoria Pike
segments.text: Eleven miles, in a hired chaise, with a gentleman this parish has not clapped eyes on since the year nine. My dear, I do not doubt him and I do not doubt you, and that is nothing at all to the purpose. It is what is said. Send the curate.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Mr Rowe cannot swear to my brother's hand.

segments.speaker: Mrs Honoria Pike
segments.text: Then send Owen.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Owen would not sleep for a week and would say so in the office. Ma'am, I am seven and twenty and I keep house for an apothecary. There is very little left of me to be ruined that Amberlight has not already had the pleasure of.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mr Rowe paid for the chaise out of two pounds he had by him for the vestry glazing, and said the glazier could wait until Lady Day, and would not be thanked for it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They went at ten. The road was cut up from the week's rain and the near hind wheel had been complaining since the Alresford turning, and about three miles short of the city it stopped complaining and went. The chaise came down slowly and sideways into the ditch grass, and the dispensing book slid off Judith's lap into the straw, and nobody was hurt at all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The driver got the horses' heads and walked back to look at what was left of the felloe.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: Can it be got on again?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The driver crouched, turned a splinter of the rim over in his fingers, and threw it into the ditch.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: Then what passes this road tonight?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The driver straightened up and looked west, where the light was already going out of the fields. Nothing passed here now, he said, till the market carts in the morning. The wheelwright at Itchen Vale was a mile and a half off, and would not come out after dark for any money in Hampshire.
